scope: Exact static-source argument review. This is not a whole-screen visual conformance certificate. Unknown records remain actionable and no whitelist is inferred.

rules.central-copy: PARTS source/body/fingerprint equivalence verified before each copied argument is classified.
rules.central-selector: The exact static class selector has a declaration in a currently hashed central CSS recipe.
rules.canonical-scalar: The entire scalar value is a sequence of declared central CSS variables or an exact imported object member traced to such variables. Mixed expressions are not inferred. Changed scale-helper semantics or any local shadowing remain unknown.
rules.numeric-adapter: Direct BP, LAYOUT, ICON or QDRuntime access imports the verified centrally distributed runtime module.
rules.proven-composition: Every conditional result, template interpolation or object property independently resolves to a central value or an explicit structural keyword. Unknown spreads and authored literal fragments block the entire composition.
rules.font-resource: Generated font-face declarations identify shipped binary resources; family selection remains controlled by central tokens.
rules.css-structure: A proven JSX style/CSSProperties object contains a reviewed dimensionless layout, alignment, text wrapping or reset value.
rules.expert-count-data: The exact spread builds an expert id/email/count record, then sorts it by count; it is not style composition.
rules.data-envelope: The exact complete binding is a native Date, native HTTP Response or fingerprint-reviewed JSON success/failure envelope. Descendant values and subsequent visual uses are still separately inventoried.
rules.inactive-export-graph: The explicitly named compatibility exports have no runtime consumers in the freshly parsed application graph. Aliases, namespace escapes, dynamic module loading and indirect references invalidate this proof. This is not central ownership of visible styles.
rules.unknown: No sufficient exact-source proof exists in this review. Further inspection or centralization is required.
